parts.prompt: Name the chamber that receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
parts.answerKey: Deoxygenated blood from the body first enters the right atrium.

parts.prompt: Which chamber pumps this blood to the lungs, and through which vessel?
parts.answerKey: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.

parts.prompt: Name the chamber that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
parts.answerKey: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs to the left atrium through pulmonary veins.

parts.prompt: Which chamber pumps oxygenated blood to the body, and through which vessel?
parts.answerKey: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta.

parts.prompt: State how the septum helps circulation.
parts.answerKey: The septum prevents mixing and supports efficient double circulation.

answerKey.modelAnswer:
Deoxygenated blood from the body first enters the right atrium.
The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs to the left atrium through pulmonary veins.
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta.
The septum prevents mixing and supports efficient double circulation.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium and right ventricle; it is pumped to the lungs through the pulmonary artery; oxygenated blood returns through pulmonary veins to the left atrium and left ventricle; the left ventricle pumps it through the aorta to the body.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Oxygen concentration is higher in alveolar air than deoxygenated blood; oxygen diffuses across the thin alveolar-capillary surface into blood; carbon dioxide diffuses in the opposite direction; ventilation and blood flow maintain the concentration gradient.

questions.prompt: Explain the events during inhalation.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.

answerKey.modelAnswer: The diaphragm contracts and flattens; external intercostal muscles raise the ribs; thoracic volume increases and pressure in the lungs falls; air enters down the pressure gradient.

alternatives.prompt: Explain the events during exhalation.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Glomerular filtration transfers water and small solutes into Bowman’s capsule; blood cells and most proteins remain in capillaries; glucose, amino acids, salts and required water are reabsorbed; remaining wastes form urine.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Soluble products of photosynthesis are loaded into phloem; loading requires energy; translocation occurs between source and sink regions; food is unloaded at growing or storage regions.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.

alternatives.prompt: Describe the route of oxygenated blood from lungs to body.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to form carbohydrates and oxygen; respiration uses food and oxygen to release energy; respiration forms carbon dioxide and water; these products can be reused in photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Describe the functions of amylase, pepsin and lipase.

source.reference: ExamGuru-authored CBSE Class X Science 2026–27 question mapped to the specified blueprint slot.
